newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen sharply lower on Nikkei surge.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen sharply lower on Nikkei surge.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures on TIFFE were sharply lower by midday following a surge in Tokyo stocks and a sharp fall in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, traders said.
The key contract ended the morning at the intraday low of 98.92. Turnover was 73,059 lots.
"December euroyen fell sharply as stocks jumped. The Nikkei's rise above 20,000 could strengthen the argument in favour of raising interest rates," said a city bank trader.
At midday, the Nikkei 225 stock average was up 689.77 points, or 3.53 percent, at 20,204.52.
A sharp fall in JGB futures also weighed on euroyen futures, traders said.
Key June JGB futures ended the morning down 1.17 at 124.33.
"Selling pressure in euroyen futures intensified after June JGB futures fell below the key support point of 124.70 in late morning," said a trust bank trader.
Traders said December euroyen futures could fall further in the afternoon but some buying interest may emerge near 98.90.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was mostly traded at 0.49 percent, up from Friday's weighted average of 0.47 percent, traders said.
Japan's financial markets were closed on Monday for a national holiday.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) drained a net 100 billion yen from the money market on Tuesday morning. The money market was in surplus by about 390 billion yen going into the day.

Traders said money market rates were facing upward pressure despite the central bank's accommodative stance, as a large amount of certificates of deposits (CDs) is due to mature after the "Golden Week" holiday period, which ended on Monday.
Traders also said that suppliers of funds remained reluctant to lower their offer rates.
About 10 billion yen worth of three-month CDs was issued at 0.57 percent on Tuesday morning. The CDs were issued at 0.56 and 0.57 percent last Friday.
No new one-month or two-month CDs were issued this morning. They were being offered at 0.54 percent, unchanged from Friday.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, IRS rates were higher, particularly at the longer end of the yield curve, due to a sharp fall in JGBs.
Two-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.18/1.22 percent, up from Friday's 1.10/1.14 percent. Five-year IRS rates were at 2.05/2.09 percent, up from Friday's 1.92/1.96 percent.
Ten-year IRS rates were quoted at 2.89/2.93 percent, up sharply from 2.75/2.79 percent last Friday.
